ja: בה' ועשה טוב שכן ארץ ורעה אמונה, וקאל טוב ה' לקויו לנפש תדרשנו. ואמא מן תוכל עלי אללה והו יעציה, פמא אג'הלה ומא אקל עקלה ותמייזה, אד' ירי אן מן תוכל לה מן אלנאס באמר, אד'א אלזמה אלקיאם בחאג'ה מן חואיג'ה או נהאה ען אמר וכ'אלף מא חד לה ואתצל באלוכיל ד'לך, כאן נקצ'ה לאמרה אקוי אסבאב חרמאנה לקצ'א מא תוכל עליה פיה. ואחרי ואוכד מן תג'אוז חדוד אללה ופראיצ'ה אלתי ועד ואועד עליהא אן יכ'ייב רג'א אלמתוכל עליה אד'א עצאה, ולם יסתחק אסם מתוכל עלי אללה, בל הו כקול אלכתאב כי מה תקות חנף כי יבצע כי ישל אלוה נפשו, הצעקתו ישמע אל, וקאל הגנוב רצוח ונאוף והשבע לשקר וקטר לבעל והולך אחרי אלהים אחרים אשר לא ידעתם ובאתם ועמדתם לפני בבית הזה אשר נקרא שמי עליו ואמרתם נצלנו למען עשות את כל התועבות האלה, המערת פריצים היה הבית הזה אשר נקרא שמי עליו. ואלמקדמה אלכ'אמסה אן יצח ענדה אן תמאם אלאמור אלחאדת'ה פי הד'א אלעאלם בעד אלכ'ליקה באמרין, אחדהמא אקדאר אלכ'אלק תעאלי ומשיתה לכ'רוג'הא אלי חדוד אלכון מן אלעדם. ואלת'אני אסבאב ווסאיט מנהא קריבה ומנהא בעידה, ומנהא ט'אהרה ומנהא באטנה, וג'מיעהא ג'אריה אלי תתמים מא קדר כונה וט'הורה בעון אללה להא עלי ד'לך. ומת'ל אלאסבאב אלקריבה, פי אסתכ'ראג' אלמא מן עמק אלארץ' באלדולאב פי אלקואידס אלתי תרפע אלמא באלסאניה מן אלביר, ואמא סבבה אלבעיד פאלאנסאן אלד'י יקרן אלדאבה באלסאניה פתחרכהא לרפע אלמא מן קער אלביר אלי סטח אלארץ', ואמא אלאסבאב

For instance, we see one grain of wheat, from which sprout three hundred ears, in each ear about thirty grains — so that one grain becomes the cause of ten thousand grains and thereabouts. Is the weakness of the grain hidden, given the like of this? And so for the rest of the seeded and planted grains. Likewise the speech concerning the coming-to-be of the body of the human and the rest of the animal from a drop of seed; and like it, the bringing-into-being of a great fish from the egg of a fish, in its weakness. The preoccupation of the soul with advancing what God has delayed, and delaying what He has advanced, and multiplying what He has made little, and diminishing what He has multiplied, of the goods of this world — apart from causing-oneself to fulfill the obligations of His obedience and to bind oneself to His Law — is a weakness of discrimination concerning the true reality of His knowledge, and an ignorance of the goodness of His care for us. The Wise One has gestured at this concept with his saying: "For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under the heavens" (Ecclesiastes 3:1). Then he mentioned twenty-eight concepts under it, namely his saying: "A time to be born and a time to die" up to "a time of war and a time of peace" (Ecclesiastes 3:2–8); and he said: "For time and chance happen to them all" (Ecclesiastes 9:11); and he said: "For high one is above high one watches, and there are higher ones above them" (Ecclesiastes 5:7). The currents of the judgments of the Creator (exalted be He) are more hidden, more concealed, and more exalted than that we should reach knowledge of their particulars — let alone their universals; and Scripture has said: "For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts" (Isaiah 55:9).

**The second premise** — his knowledge and verification that God (mighty and exalted) is overseeing him, and nothing is hidden from Him of his outer and inner, his secret and his manifest, of his purification in his reliance upon his Lord or the absence of his purification in it — as Scripture said, "The Lord knows the thoughts of man, that they are vapor" (Psalms 94:11); and He said, "Behold, He weighs hearts; does He not understand?" (Proverbs 24:12); and He said, "For You alone know the heart of all the children of man" (1 Kings 8:39). When the one relying has verified this, it does not become valid for him to claim reliance on God (exalted be He) by his speech without his relying on Him with his heart and his inner being; for he would then be of the rank of the one of whom it was said: "With his mouth and his lips they have honored Me, but their heart is far from Me" (Isaiah 29:13).

**The third premise** — singling out his Lord by reliance upon Him in what reliance is incumbent upon him in, and not associating another with Him in it — so that he relies upon Him together with one of created beings, by which his reliance upon God would be corrupted, since he has associated another with Him. You have learned what Scripture said about Asa, despite his bounty, when he leaned upon physicians, in his saying: "And in his sickness he did not seek the Lord, but the physicians" (2 Chronicles 16:12), and he was punished for this. And Scripture said: "Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and whose trust is the Lord" (Jeremiah 17:7). It is known that anyone among people who has appointed two trustees for the carrying-out of one of his affairs — or more than that — his reliance is corrupted; how much more so the one who has relied on God and on something other than Him: he has corrupted his reliance, and that becomes the strongest cause of his being denied the carrying-out of what he relied upon Him for, as Scripture said: "Cursed is the man who trusts in man, and makes flesh his arm" (Jeremiah 17:5).
